passage:
Counsellor's note, after the parent visit on Wednesday. Anand, a father, came in worried about how to tell his nine-year-old, Bela, that Nani was very ill and that the family would be visiting the hospital often. I sat in while he told her at the school bench. He did not say Nani was "resting". He said, "Nani is very sick. The doctors are working hard to help her. Nobody caused it, and it's okay to be sad. You can ask me anything."
Bela was quiet, then asked, "Will she come home?" Anand said, "We don't know yet, and I will tell you what I know." Bela leaned against his arm.
Sarika, school counsellor

qa.q: How old is Bela?
qa.a: Bela is nine years old.

qa.q: What might Bela have been feeling when asking "Will she come home?"
qa.a: Bela was probably scared and wanted to know the truth. Leaning against Anand's arm shows a need for closeness.

qa.q: What did Anand do that helped Bela trust him?
qa.a: Anand used plain words, said Nobody caused it and invited questions. When he did not know the answer, he said so instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How might Anand have felt while telling Bela about Nani?
qa.a: Anand was probably worried and sad, and also determined to be honest. Coming in for support beforehand shows how hard it was.

grounding: A parent tells a child in simple terms why a relative is ill, and honesty at the child's level builds trust.

passage:
Sunday night. Told Parul, my nine-year-old, about the move today. I was dreading it. I sat on her bed and said, "Parul, my new job is in another city. We are moving in June. You will go to a new school." I did not say "it will be fun, don't worry." I said I was a little scared too.
She cried. Then she asked, "Will I have to leave my best friend Meghna?" I said yes, and that Meghna and she can call every Sunday. She asked about her room, her books, the cat. I answered each question, even the ones I didn't know: "I'll find out."
She fell asleep holding my hand. I felt tired and lighter.
— Amandeep

qa.q: When are Amandeep and Parul moving?
qa.a: They are moving in June.

qa.q: What was Amandeep feeling before telling Parul about the move?
qa.a: Amandeep was dreading it and felt a little scared. Saying "I was dreading it" and admitting the fear to Parul show honest nerves.

qa.q: What did Amandeep do that gave Parul the truth without overwhelming her?
qa.a: Amandeep gave plain facts, said it was a little scary too and answered each question, even saying "I'll find out". No cheerful cover story was offered.

qa.q: What might Parul have felt when asking "Will I have to leave my best friend Meghna?"
qa.a: Parul was probably sad and worried about losing a friend. Hearing that they could call every Sunday gave some comfort.

grounding: A person tells their nine-year-old plainly why the family is moving, answering questions honestly at the child's level.

passage:
In the village, the doctor's jeep had come twice in one week, and nine-year-old Chaitanya had started lying awake. He heard whispers at night: "hospital," "the town," "we'll see." In the morning everyone smiled too much.
One evening, his mother, Rashmi, found him sitting on the cattle-shed wall, very still.
"Chaitu, you're worried about Dadaji."
He nodded. "Is he going to die?"
Rashmi sat beside him. "Dadaji's heart is tired and weak, and the doctor wants him in the big hospital in town so they can watch him closely. We don't know everything yet. When I know more, I'll tell you. I promise."
Chaitanya thought. "I thought it was worse. Because everyone was whispering."
"No more whispering. You can ask me anything."
"Can I go see him?"
"Sunday. We'll take the bus together."

qa.q: Where did Rashmi find Chaitanya?
qa.a: She found him sitting on the cattle-shed wall.

qa.q: Why had Chaitanya started lying awake?
qa.a: He was frightened and anxious about Dadaji, because the whispers and forced smiles made him imagine something worse.

qa.q: What did Rashmi do well in explaining?
qa.a: Rashmi told him simply and honestly that Dadaji's heart is weak, admitted they didn't know everything, and promised to share news.

qa.q: How might Rashmi feel after the talk?
qa.a: Rashmi likely felt relieved and closer to Chaitanya, knowing the whispering had been making his fear worse.

grounding: A parent tells a child simply and honestly why a grandparent is ill, easing fears that secrecy had fed.

passage:
In their Haifa apartment, Yosef had noticed the boxes in the storeroom and the long phone calls behind closed doors. For a week the ten-year-old had been quiet, eating little.
Daniel finally sat on the edge of his bed. "Yosef, you look worried. Want to tell me?"
"Are you and Ima getting divorced?" Yosef whispered.
Daniel's chest tightened. "No. No, we're not. I'm sorry you've been carrying that." He took a breath. "Here's what's really happening. I got a new job in Toronto. We're moving there in August. The boxes are for that. We didn't tell you because we weren't sure yet, and that was a mistake."
Yosef stared. "Toronto? Is there snow?"
"Lots."
"Will I have friends?"
"Not at first. It'll be hard. We'll help."
Yosef let out a long breath and leaned against his father.

qa.q: When is the family moving to Toronto?
qa.a: They are moving there in August.

qa.q: What was Yosef afraid of before Daniel explained?
qa.a: Yosef was scared and anxious that his parents were getting divorced, imagining the worst from the boxes and closed doors.

qa.q: What went right in how Daniel explained the move?
qa.a: He asked about Yosef's worry first, told the truth simply, admitted keeping quiet was a mistake, and was honest that making friends would be hard.

qa.q: What would change if Daniel had kept the move secret longer?
qa.a: Yosef's divorce fear would likely have grown, and he might have trusted his parents less when he finally found out.

grounding: A parent tells a child simply why the family is moving, and honesty replaces a worse story the child had imagined.

passage:
In the hospital waiting room in Hyderabad, Aditi swung her legs and watched the nurses hurry past. She had been told only that they were "visiting Nani". But Nani was in a bed with tubes, and Mummy's eyes were red.
"Mummy, did I make Nani sick? I jumped on her bed last week."
Kalyani knelt in front of her. "No, beta. Nothing you did made Nani sick." She chose her words carefully. "Nani's kidneys are very tired. Kidneys clean the blood, like a filter cleans water. Hers aren't cleaning well, so the machine is helping. The doctors are looking after her."
"Will she come home?"
"We hope so. I don't know yet. When the doctors tell me, I'll tell you."
Aditi thought. "Can I draw her a picture of a filter?"
Kalyani laughed through her tears. "She'd love that."

qa.q: What did Kalyani compare Nani's kidneys to?
qa.a: She said kidneys clean the blood, like a filter cleans water.

qa.q: Why did Aditi ask if she had made Nani sick?
qa.a: Aditi felt guilty and worried, and without a real explanation she imagined that jumping on Nani's bed had caused the illness.

qa.q: Which of Kalyani's choices built trust?
qa.a: She knelt to Aditi's level, said clearly it wasn't Aditi's fault, explained in simple words, and was honest that she didn't know everything yet.

qa.q: How might Nani feel receiving Aditi's picture?
qa.a: Nani would likely feel loved and cheered by Aditi's drawing.

grounding: A parent tells a child in simple, honest terms why a grandparent is ill, replacing an imagined, guilty story.

passage: I'm Bhupen, Akash's cousin, staying with them that month. For a week Akash had been strange: leaving his fish, whispering at night, "Are we in trouble? Did Papa do something bad?" Nobody had told him anything. On Sunday his Papa sat on Akash's bed. "Your mind's been busy, hasn't it? Here's the truth. My office in Jorhat is closing. I've got work in Guwahati, so in June we all move there. New school. We'll come back for Bihu to see Koka and Aita." Akash asked three quick questions: would his cycle come, was there a river, could he still call Dipankar. Papa answered each one. Then Akash lay back. "I thought it was something much worse." That night he ate two helpings of rice.

qa.q: Where will the family move in June?
qa.a: To Guwahati.

qa.q: What was Akash worried about before Papa explained?
qa.a: Akash was anxious and scared that the family was in trouble or that Papa had done something bad.

qa.q: Which parts of Papa's explanation helped, and why?
qa.a: Simple true reasons, the office closing and the new job, a clear month, a plan for visits, and an answer to each quick question, which ended the worse story Akash had imagined.

qa.q: How did Bhupen see the change in Akash after the talk?
qa.a: Bhupen saw Akash relax, admit fearing something much worse, and eat two helpings of rice that night.

grounding: Shows a parent telling a child in simple, honest terms why the family is moving, which ends the worse story the child had been imagining.
